sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant/convict would submit that the appellant/convict was of tender age of 19 years at the time of the alleged incident.

He would further submit that in her statement recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. before the Magistrate, the victim/prosecutrix has specifically stated that she knew the appellant/convict for the last two years; that on 02.12.2019, the physical relationship were established between them only once; that, the victim was in friendship with the appellant/convict and they used to talk with each other.

He would further submit that if, at all, there was any relationship between the appellant/convict and the victim that was because of the mutual infatuation for each other that is generally found in the people of this tender age.
He would further submit that in her examination-in-chief, the victim has stated that the appellant/convict was known to her for the last two years.

He would further submit that the appellant/convict was on bail during trial and he did not misuse the same; that, concluding of the appeal would take long time, therefore, the appellant/convict may be granted bail 6.

Per contra, learned State counsel vehemently opposed the bail application, however, he would CRLA/253/2024 on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67372498/
1 admit that the appellant/convict was 19 years old at the time of the incident and he was on bail during the trial and did not misuse the liberty of bail 7.
Having considered the entirety of the facts and without expressing any final opinion on the merits of the case, the appellant/convict is admitted to bail.

8. Let the appellant/convict be released on bail, during the pendency of present criminal appeal, on furnishing bail bond with two sureties in the amount of 40,000/- and personal bond of the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court.
9.
Application for Bail and Suspension of Sentence (IA 2 of 2024) stands disposed of accordingly.

10. List this case on 27.12.2024 for final hearing.
